text: Not all men, but if I gave you a box of Whoppers and I told you that one out of every 10 of them was actually a piece of human sh** rolled into a ball and dipped in chocolate, you'd be wary of all of them, would you not? That's what I thought. Okay, let's go with your example. Let's say I did get a box of 10 Whoppers and one of them is a piece of sh** dipped in chocolate. Let's even assume I'm very hungry and for some reason that is the only food I have at home. The thing is, I'm not just going to start eating them one by one and hope for the best. I would check first. Probably get the gloves, put 10 Whoppers on a table, cut them in half, take a look. And once I find the sh** one, I throw it away. Now I have 9 normal Whoppers and I'm not going to treat those 9 like they are also contaminated. No, I treat them as normal edible Whoppers. Same goes in real life. Are there bad men? Of course they are. Are there bad women? Of course they are. And depending on what you mean by bad, it might even be more than 1 out of 10. But here's the key point. In real life, you don't have to just eat the Whoppers immediately. You can take your time, you can test people, you can observe how they behave, what they do, which values do they have. And if you find a bad one, you avoid them. You go and choose the ones that are actually decent. Because sitting there, blaming the whole box of Whoppers because one is made of sh**, that's not the solution. Learning how to tell which one is edible and which one isn't, that's the way.
